newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares rise in heavy trade on local buying.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares rise in heavy trade on local buying.

text.p: Brazilian stocks ended sharply higher on Tuesday, underpinned by domestic buy orders and a surge in benchmark Telebras, brokers said.
The Bovespa index .BVSP of the 48 most active shares closed up 2.85 percent at 12,587 points on heavy volume of 1.09 billion reais ($1.01 billion).
"There is a lot of money coming in, and most of it came from domestic equity funds and local investors," one trader said.
Traders said shares closed just slightly below the day's highs.
Telebras was the leading gainer once again, with its preferred stock surging 3.01 percent to 161 reais at the close. Its voting share traded even higher, closing at 146.30 reais, up 3.39 percent.
Some analysts said they were surprised by the market's strength, noting that a correction in prices now would be welcomed.
"I began to be concerned about the bolsa's rally. When the market will take a break?," a broker said.
So far this month, the Sao Paulo bolsa has risen over seven percent, bringing the year-to-date rise to more than 73 percent, nearly all of 1996's gains.

Analysts also said a rebound on Wall Street also helped to boost market sentiment here. U.S. stocks had dived Monday on comments by Japan's prime minister about potential Japanese sales of U.S. government bonds.
Other blue-chips also closed firm. State oil firm Petrobras jumped 4.38 percent to 310 reais, while Federal power holding company Eletrobras surged 4.22 percent to 666.99 reais.
The only exception among the blue-chips were private miner Cia. Vale do Rio Doce, which ended flat at 23.90 reais, and Banco do Brasil, which closed slightly off.
The power sector index .IEE of the nine most liquid stocks of the electrical industry closed up 4.6 percent at 3,478 points.
